sourceInformation.source: H.E.R.O. (Activision, 1984), designed by John Van Ryzin
sourceInformation.perspective: Side-on 2.5D with a scrolling orthographic camera
sourceInformation.tech: Three.js r180 (0.180.0), WebGPURenderer (WebGPU primary, WebGL2 recovery); Rapier 3D compat 0.19.3; Web Audio; Gamepad API; AI Hub client 1.4.0; esbuild 0.25.12 for packaging
sourceInformation.artDirection: Original procedural cel-shaded cave dioramas, low-poly models and ink outlines
sourceInformation.animation: Three.js AnimationMixer, AnimationClip and NumberKeyframeTrack for propeller, limbs, breathing, waving and wings; procedural secondary motion
sourceInformation.audio: Code-written oscillator music, rotor, lasers, explosions and pickups; synthesized gibberish voices. Music defaults to 10%.
sourceInformation.online: AI Hub shared-world host-authoritative co-op for 1–4 players; standalone shared-screen co-op for 1–2 players
sourceInformation.testing: Headless Chromium 153 / Playwright 1.63.0; software WebGPU; complete physical and attract campaign replays; gamepad emulation; multitouch phone profile; audio analyser; GPU recovery; AI Hub 2/4-player harness with 150 ms latency, 50 ms jitter and 5% loss, host leaving and a separate host. Physical hardware and human listening: unknown.
sourceInformation.research: Original Activision manual, Atarimania screenshot and metadata, Activisions newsletter propeller-sound description; exact original recording fidelity unknown

testingFeedback: 7 distinct issues: a Rapier startup API mismatch, a blinking title pilot, two blocked replay waypoints, a negative-power edge case, overlapping touch guidance, and a headless Vulkan presentation configuration issue. All corrected. Test-script assertion mistakes are excluded.
1 game-breaking issue: the initial Rapier method mismatch prevented startup. It is fixed.
The complete campaign traversal with Rapier collisions enabled found two blocked route waypoints. Invulnerability was enabled for that traversal.
Initial headless WebGPU screenshots with incomplete Chromium Vulkan flags showed a blank canvas and hid the scene.
engineFeedback: Native AnimationMixer clips and MeshToonMaterial work well with procedural models and WebGPU in a self-contained HTML file.
Yes: I initially used a nonexistent Rapier enableSlide method instead of setSlideEnabled, and had to correct the headless Vulkan presentation flags.
The complete rescue state machine and host-authoritative co-op synchronization, plus controller-first menus and synthesized audio.
Verifying WebGPU presentation and resource lifetimes in software-rendered browser sessions, especially multiple copies.
none; engine libraries are unmodified. Device-loss recovery is application code.
Clearer built-in WebGPU device-loss diagnostics and a reliable documented headless capture recipe.
promptFeedback: Concrete source fidelity, controller-first UX, attract-mode and multiplayer/testing acceptance criteria.
Standalone multiplayer transport was unspecified; I chose 1–2 local shared-screen pilots plus 1–4 networked pilots through AI Hub.
Finishing and testing four distinct descents, every input type, procedural audio and shared-world networking in one file.
Specify standalone local versus internet multiplayer, and clarify whether automatic WebGL2 fallback is acceptable.

aiHub.name: H.E.R.O. After Hours
aiHub.tagline: The night shift needs a lift.
aiHub.description: Clock in with a prop-pack, helmet laser and a pocketful of dynamite. Rescue eight night-shift miners through four inked cave descents, alone or with colleagues.
aiHub.controls: Move: WASD/left stick; fly: Space/Cross; laser: F or mouse/R2 (J in solo); dynamite: E/Square; pause: Esc/Options; local P2: IJKL, N, M.
